what_happened: While raising agent caps, the the person running Athena set a whole-job limit of $40. The per-stage limits they chose (reader, five planning rounds, writer, verifier) add up to $47. Admission refused the config change because the stage limits can exceed the job limit. The the person running Athena re-queued the change with a $60 job limit. No job was running, so nothing else broke.
cause: The cost limits are independent numbers in the config. Nothing derives the job limit from the stage limits or shows their sum while the the person running Athena edits them. The only consistency check runs at admission, after the change is already queued. So a person tuning several limits has to do the arithmetic in their head, and a mistake costs a refused job and a re-queue.
prevention: Add a config consistency check that computes the worst-case job cost from the stage limits (reader + planning rounds × per-round cap + writer + verifier, and any producer cap) and compares it with the whole-job limit. Run it as a pre-check in the same config validation that admission uses, and expose it as a command the the person running Athena runs before queuing a cap change. On failure it should print the sum, the job limit and the shortfall. The same validation should also run in the repo's tests, so a hand edit or a job edit cannot land an inconsistent set of limits.
proposed_request: Add a pre-queue consistency check for cost limits in athena.toml. The outcome: when the per-stage cost limits (reader, each planning round up to the configured number of rounds, writer, producer if present, verifier) add up to more than the whole-job cost limit, the config is reported as inconsistent before any job is queued. The report states the computed sum, the job limit and the shortfall. Provide it as a command the person running Athena can run on the current or a proposed athena.toml, and make the same check run in the config validation that admission uses and in the repo's tests. Acceptance: (1) a test config whose stage limits sum to $47 with a $40 job limit is reported inconsistent, naming $47, $40 and $7; (2) the same stage limits with a $60 job limit pass; (3) the live athena.toml passes; (4) the check does not pin any live config value in a test, so unrelated config edits do not break it. Update docs/decisions.md only if an existing decision about cost limits contradicts this.
